# Turn Off AI Chat History and Data Saving in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini

> **In short:** You can stop ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini from using your conversations to train future AI models by flipping a privacy toggle in each service's settings — but the exact menu names change often, and turning off training does not erase the conversations those companies have already saved.

By default, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini save your chats and may use them to train future versions of themselves. This guide shows you how to switch that off in each service — on web and mobile — and explains what each toggle actually changes, and what it quietly does not.

## Before you start
- A free or paid **personal** account on each AI service you want to adjust. Work or school accounts are usually managed by your employer and may not let you change these settings.
- A web browser is the easiest place to do this. Phone apps work too, but menus shift around more often.
- Set aside about **15 minutes total** — roughly five minutes per service.
- Make sure you are signed in to each service before you begin, so the settings actually save.

## Step 1 — Open ChatGPT's Data controls
Go to **chatgpt.com** in a browser and sign in. Open your **account menu** (click your profile picture or name), select **Settings**, then select **Data controls**.

On the ChatGPT phone app (iOS or Android), open the **sidebar**, tap your **profile icon** to open Settings, then tap **Data controls**.

You'll know it worked when you see the Data controls page with a setting called **Improve the model for everyone**.

## Step 2 — Turn off ChatGPT's training setting
Select **Improve the model for everyone**, switch it **off**, and select **Done**. On the phone app, just switch it off.

When you're signed in, this one setting applies to your account on the web and on your phone. Turning it off does **not** delete or hide your saved chats — they stay in your history. If you want a single conversation that isn't saved to your history at all, start a **Temporary chat** instead: OpenAI says these aren't used to improve its models, though they may be kept for up to 30 days for safety purposes.

You'll know it worked when **Improve the model for everyone** shows as off after you close and reopen Settings. If you can't change it, a parent or guardian setting or a work or school workspace may be controlling it.

## Step 3 — Open Claude's Privacy settings
Go to **claude.ai** and sign in. Select **your name** in the settings menu, then select **Settings**, then **Privacy**. (You can also go straight to the page at **claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls**.)

In the Claude phone app, the path is the same: select **your name**, then **Settings**, then **Privacy**.

You'll know it worked when you see a toggle labeled **Help Improve our AI models**.

## Step 4 — Turn off Claude's training toggle
Switch **Help Improve our AI models** **off**.

According to Anthropic, once this is off, your **new** chats and coding sessions won't be used for future model training. Chats you have already stored won't be used in future training runs either, but anything already included in training that had started, or in models already trained, stays there. Separately, **incognito** chats are never used to improve Claude, even when this toggle is on.

You'll know it worked when the toggle stays off after you refresh the page. If you signed in with a work or school account, your organization manages these settings.

## Step 5 — Open Gemini History
In Gemini, this setting is now called **History** (older versions of the app called it "Gemini Apps Activity"). On a computer, go to **gemini.google.com** and click **History**.

In the Gemini app on Android, tap the **menu** on the left, then your **profile picture or initial**, then **Gemini History**.

You'll know it worked when you see a page with an **On** button near the top.

## Step 6 — Turn off Gemini History
Near the top, click **On**, then choose **Turn off** — or **Turn off and delete history** if you also want your past Gemini conversations removed from your history.

Google notes that even with History off, your conversations are still kept with your account for **around two months**; they just won't appear in your Gemini History. Turning this off also doesn't change your Google Search or YouTube history, which have their own settings. If you use a work or school account, your administrator controls this setting.

You'll know it worked when the button near the top no longer says **On**.

## Common mistakes
- **Looking for a "delete my data" button.** None of these toggles erase what the company already has on file. If you want old chats removed, each service has a separate **Delete** or **Clear conversations** option — and even then, companies often keep copies for legal or safety reasons for a while.
- **Assuming one toggle fixes everything.** In Gemini especially, there are **multiple** Google activity controls. Turning off Gemini History does not affect Search history, YouTube history, or other Google products. Check each one separately if you care about all of them.
- **Trusting the toggle forever.** Companies update their settings and policies regularly. The opt-out you flipped today may quietly disappear or change meaning in six months — set a calendar reminder every few months to come back and check.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Turning these off is a good habit if you ever paste anything personal into an AI chat — names, addresses, health questions, work emails. It does not make you invisible, but it stops your words from being used to teach the next model.
- **For your business or work:** If you handle customer data, contracts, or anything confidential, do not rely on these toggles alone. Many companies explicitly say opt-outs do not cover legal requests or internal abuse detection. Use a separate AI account with synthetic data, or stick to enterprise plans that promise stronger privacy.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick the service you use the most, open its settings, and turn off the training toggle right now. That single move is the most useful thing you can do today — you can come back for the other two later.

## Try it now
Open the AI assistant you used most recently, click your profile picture, find the privacy or data settings, and turn off the training toggle. It takes about a minute, and you'll see exactly what your settings look like today.
